Standard-library runtime contracts ​

These contracts describe the current C runtime. CX allocations are managed by a non-moving conservative collector with explicit native worker registration and cooperative stop-the-world coordination and public System.Threading workers, mutexes, and atomic integer cells. The collector design and limits are documented in managed-memory-design.md. The ABI and ownership rules remain experimental.

Allocation and ownership ​

  • Memory.Alloc returns zero-initialized, collector-tracked storage. A zero-byte request returns a non-null allocation that can be passed to Memory.Free.
  • Memory.Realloc(block, 0) frees block and returns null. For a nonzero size, a failed reallocation terminates the process; it never returns a lost old pointer.
  • Memory.Copy is a no-op for size zero. Nonzero copies require valid, non-overlapping ranges, as with C memcpy.
  • Built-in T[] storage and the public System.Collections.Array&lt;T&gt; API use the same System.Collections.Array runtime structure and own a zero-initialized element buffer allocated by cx_array_new. The public type is declared in src/System/Collections/Array.cx and exposes Length, Get, and Set. The current explicit cleanup is Memory.Free(array-&gt;_data) followed by Memory.Free(array). cx_array_at returns null for a null array, an out-of-range index, invalid zero-sized elements, or missing backing storage.
  • Runtime-owned allocations go through Memory.Alloc and are eligible for collection when unreachable. Memory.Free immediately unregisters and releases a block; freeing a block while a live reference may be used is invalid. Memory.Realloc tracks the resized block, but references invalidated by a move must not be used.
  • Nullable is a one-pointer value. Its constructor and Value setter store a non-owning pointer; compiler-generated lifts call Nullable&lt;T&gt;.CreateValueStorage, which allocates a copy of the supplied bytes through Memory.Alloc; the payload is traced conservatively with the rest of the managed heap.
  • Object initializes its runtime vtable. Ordinary objects leave _box null; boxed value objects use it to retain their managed box header and payload. No finalizers run. The non-moving collector may retain unreachable blocks when stale pointer-shaped values remain on a scanned stack or in a registered root.
  • DateTime component construction validates the Gregorian date and time fields. AddMonths uses calendar months, clamps the day to the last day of the destination month, and keeps the time-of-day and offset. Invalid components and results outside the stored millisecond range write a diagnostic and exit with failure.

Strings, characters, and console ​

  • String data is UTF-8 and _length is a byte count. String.Length counts Unicode scalar values, and String.Item indexes those scalar values. The item getter returns -1 for an invalid index or malformed UTF-8 sequence. Length counts each malformed byte as one replacement position so it stays bounded by the stored byte length.
  • String ==, String !=, Equals, and GetHashCode use the stored UTF-8 bytes; equal byte sequences compare equal and produce the same hash. ToString() returns the same string instance. String constructors initialize the String vtable after the base Object constructor initializes the base object state.
  • String &lt;, &lt;=, &gt;, and &gt;= compare UTF-8 byte sequences lexicographically. For valid UTF-8, this gives Unicode scalar value ordering. A null string sorts before a non-null string when the comparison is made through typed string values.
  • String + String copies both UTF-8 byte sequences into a new managed string. A null operand contributes no bytes. Length overflow and allocation failure terminate according to the runtime allocation contract.
  • String.__constructor(length, data) borrows an immutable byte buffer. The buffer must remain alive and unchanged while the string uses it. String literals borrow static storage. The character-fill constructor allocates its encoded UTF-8 buffer; callers may release it with Memory.Free only when no live reference can use it.
  • Char is a Unicode scalar value in a 32-bit integer. Char.NumBytes returns its UTF-8 encoded width, or -1 for a surrogate or value above U+10FFFF. Current IsDigit, IsLetter, case conversion, and whitespace helpers are ASCII-only.
  • Console.Read(length) reads at most length bytes. ReadLine() reads through a newline or EOF and grows its buffer as needed. Both return a heap-allocated String object with heap-allocated contents; those allocations are traced. Callers may release them with Memory.Free when no live reference can use them. Console.Write writes the stored UTF-8 bytes unchanged and returns the number of bytes written.

Allocation failures in Memory.Alloc and nonzero Memory.Realloc write Out of memory to standard error and exit with failure. The old allocation remains untouched when reallocation fails before process termination. Bounds, ownership, and UTF-8 errors do not currently raise typed CX exceptions.

Shared-library declarations ​

CX_API marks runtime functions as exports while building cxcore, imports for dynamic consumers, and undecorated declarations for static consumers. Public runtime data uses CX_CXCORE_DATA_API with the same producer/consumer/static behavior. CMake propagates CX_STATIC_LINK from static cxcore targets to their consumers.

Managed-memory limits ​

The collector scans registered thread stacks, saved registers, managed blocks, and registered static-field regions. Generated modules register their static fields; native C code must register static storage that retains managed pointers. Heap operations from an unregistered OS thread fail. Native workers must attach, poll safepoints, park during native-only blocking calls, and detach before exit; see threading-gc-design.md. Application fields require their own synchronization. Synchronous native calls on a running attached thread retain their stack roots; references retained beyond the call must be kept in a registered root or another managed block. Foreign callbacks use owned attachment scopes and removable root handles; reentry from a parked native-only blocking callback still requires a future explicit adapter.

Platform support ​

The runtime supports Windows through MSVC and x64 Linux through GCC. Linux selects native environment and system-clock providers and the platform-specific managed-memory helpers. Static and shared Linux targets build and pass the native runtime test suite in the repository's Docker development container. macOS remains unsupported.

Native interop and text ​

wchar is a 16-bit UTF-16 code unit on every target. System.WideString owns immutable copied storage; Length/Item count units and ScalarCount/ScalarAt validate scalars. Equality, hashing and ordinal comparison use units. Empty values and embedded zeros are preserved. String.ToWideString and the Object.ToString override on WideString transcode explicitly, without normalization or implicit conversion. Malformed UTF-8 or unpaired UTF-16 throws EncodingException with a byte/unit Position.

System.Interop.NativeBuffer owns malloc storage. AllocateAligned takes a power-of-two alignment for stronger SDK layouts. FromUtf8/FromUtf16 copy input with optional termination; ByteLength includes that terminator. ToUtf8String/ToWideString copy explicit output lengths without scanning for zero. Dispose is explicit/idempotent; never dispose while native code retains Data. SDK objects and buffers require their own allocator/destructor, not Memory.Alloc or NativeBuffer.Dispose.

NativeLibrary keeps loaded handles until process exit; Resolve<T> returns typed native functions or throws a load/symbol error. NativeError holds immediate TLS errno/last-error snapshots. NativeCallback.Register<T> roots a closure and optional owner until successful SDK unregistration and completion of in-flight callbacks. Unregister failure permits retry; self-unregistration is rejected. LastException survives close, and late callbacks receive their configured failure result. Small context tombstones stay until process exit; managed payloads are freed on close. Callbacks catch CX exceptions before foreign frames and restore native TLS state. See native-interop-design.md for ABI and lifetime rules.
